title: Sheafified finite-quotient scalar cochains and their augmentation
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, a finite intermediate field $E$, and $F\in\{E,\Omega\}$. Set $A(S)=C(S,F)$ with all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], on the small coherent profinite site of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group all of whose finite continuous quotients have order prime to $\ell$, with trivial action on $F$. For $n\geq0$ let $L_{pre}^n(S)$ be the $A(S)$-module of functions in $C(S\times K^n,F)$ which factor in the group coordinates through $(K/U)^n$ for some open normal subgroup $U$ of $K$. Put $L_{pre}^n=0$ for $n<0$. Restriction is pullback in $S$. Use the trivial-action inhomogeneous differential, with $d^0=0$ and
$$(dc)(s;g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=c(s;g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})+\sum_{a=1}^{n}(-1)^a c(s;g_1,\ldots,g_ag_{a+1},\ldots,g_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}c(s;g_1,\ldots,g_n).$$
Write $\mathcal L_F^\bullet(K)$ for degreewise sheafification, as ordinary internal $A$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], with its induced differential. Let $u_L:A[0]\to\mathcal L_F^\bullet(K)$ be the identity in degree zero and zero in every other degree, where $[0]$ means concentration in degree zero. The actual morphism
$$Q(u_L):A[0]\longrightarrow Q(\mathcal L_F^\bullet(K))$$
is an isomorphism in the ordinary derived category [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], where $Q$ localizes at quasi-isomorphisms. More precisely, for every $n\geq1$ and every local cocycle section of $\mathcal L_F^n(K)$, there is a covering family on which it has representatives $\bar c\in C(S_i\times Q_i^n,F)$, with $Q_i=K/U_i$ finite, satisfying $d\bar c=0$. The cover and open normal subgroups can be refined simultaneously for a representative and its cocycle equation. Each such representative has the continuous primitive
$$b(s;g_1,\ldots,g_{n-1})=\frac{(-1)^n}{|Q_i|}\sum_{h\in Q_i}\bar c(s;g_1,\ldots,g_{n-1},h),\qquad db=\bar c,$$
which factors through the same finite quotient in the remaining group variables. These primitives witness equality of the image and kernel sheaves in every positive degree. For $n=1$ every such cocycle is zero. In degree zero $\mathcal L_F^0(K)=A$ and $d^0=0$; there are no negative terms. The statements include empty test sets and $K=1$. All scalars and cochains retain the norm topology; no completeness, infinite average, or replacement of $\Omega$-valued functions by finite-subextension-valued functions is imposed.

proof.text: Obtain the continuous-cochain complex C, its finite-quotient subcomplex P, its degreewise sheafification L, the coordinates e and the comparison iota from lem-sfb-prime-to-ell-cochain-finite-quotient-descent. Use only this coordinate and sheafification data, not the derived-isomorphism conclusion. Define the additive coordinates of P by composing e with its injective inclusion. Define eta by the actual abelian sheafification unit followed by a.hom. The adjunction identities and the specified counit formula give eta followed by iota equal to the inclusion of P. Sheafification preserves monomorphisms, so iota and eta are injective. Naturality gives the restriction and differential formulas.

proof.text: For a positive-degree cocycle factoring through K/U, apply the finite clause of lem-sfb-scalar-cochain-averaging-primitives directly on K with the same U. The normed Q_ell-algebra is ultrametric, the compact totally disconnected group has an open normal basis, and hK gives the prime-to-ell quotient orders. The primitive is the required signed last-variable finite sum. Pullback along the surjective quotient map commutes with the inhomogeneous differential, so the quotient primitive has differential cbar. In degree one, the degree-zero differential is zero, hence cbar is zero. The exact finite-quotient image of P supplies the primitive as a P-section.

proof.text: The image sieve of eta over a given section is covering, by Mathlib local surjectivity of the sheafification unit. For a sheaf cocycle, lift locally to P; naturality and the already proved injectivity of eta force its differential to vanish in P. Intersect its quotient subgroup with the arbitrary prescribed U0 and precompose the representative with the quotient homomorphism. Surjectivity of that quotient transfers the cocycle equation. This yields all the required local representatives on one covering without a second cover for local equality.

proof.text: Every presheaf cocycle in positive degree has a primitive by the same finite calculation. Mathlib objectwise exactness of additive-group presheaves and exact abelian sheafification give exactness of the sheafified complex. Transport along a and reflect exactness through the faithful exact forgetful functor from internal A-modules. For the scalar identity of eta, compose with the monomorphism iota, use linearity of iota under the section-module functor, and apply the coordinate scalar identity of C.

proof.text: Evaluation at the unique empty group tuple identifies C in degree zero with the regular A-module. Its linearity uses the compatibility of the monoid multiplication of an abelian ring sheaf with multiplication of ring sections (the proved source-library lemma Sheaf.μ_sheafToPresheaf_comp_map_mul_sheafCompose). All degree-zero cochains factor through the trivial quotient, so P to C and iota are isomorphisms in degree zero. Define z by these isomorphisms, prove the degree-zero differential vanishes, and form the actual augmentation by CochainComplex.fromSingle₀Equiv. Its degree zero is z and every higher component is zero. It is a quasi-isomorphism: in degree zero use the short-complex criterion, and in every positive degree use exactness. Extension by zero preserves quasi-isomorphisms; DerivedCategory.Q inverts the extended map. Apply the argument separately to E and Omega. All constructions and formulas include empty S and trivial K, with no completeness assumption.
